races.name: Summer Saturday Series At Doncaster Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jumeirah Storm
runners_data.comment: Shaped with considerable promise on his debut at Salisbury when 2l fourth in a novice, though that effort didn’t reflect the full extent of what he may be capable of. Effective at 6f on good ground and second on our figures; he is the main threat to the selection.

runners_data.name: Keep Kicking On
runners_data.comment: Third at Haydock on his most recent run, beaten 4¼l in a novice having built on a moderate debut; he is expected to continue progressing. Effective at 6f on soft ground; a midfield contender on our figures with room for further development.

runners_data.name: Launch Sequence
runners_data.comment: A £160,000 breeze-up Mehmas colt from a top trainer, he is closely related to a smart 6f performer and his dam was useful at a mile. Our top-rated runner on debut and with connections that place horses effectively first time out, he should be the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Mobadir
runners_data.comment: Yet to trouble the principals in two starts, he produced comparable form to his debut when 3¼l adrift at Goodwood last time; the level shown is fair for a novice. Wears a first-time hood and is effective at 5/6f on soft and good; third on our figures and worth including.

runners_data.name: No More Pino
runners_data.comment: Stumbled on debut at Salisbury, beaten 8½l in a novice; the stumble may have somewhat exaggerated the defeat but it was still a limited performance. Returns wearing a hood and has scope for improvement, though he sits near the foot of our market and faces a tough task.

runners_data.name: Sultan Darius
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his debut at Windsor, beaten 6l in a maiden while wearing a tongue-tie; a solid opening effort and improvement is anticipated on this sort of surface. Effective at 6f on good to firm; his profile suggests he has a genuine chance of going well here.

runners_data.name: War Gaming
runners_data.comment: An £85,000 Mehmas gelding who is a half-brother to Gaasyah, fair at 7f, with a dam that showed her best over 5f as a juvenile. Wears first-time cheekpieces and the trainer is in good form; the pedigree is of interest but this looks a tough debut assignment.

runners_data.name: Agrippa
runners_data.comment: A 55,000gns Naval Crown colt who is a half-brother to Swan Band, useful at a mile, and out of a dam who also excelled at 8f as a juvenile. The pedigree profile is encouraging and he merits respect on his debut here.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Ayr last time, beaten 4l over 6f on softer ground, having shown clear progression from his debut. There is more to offer but the quicker surface here may be a reservation; a genuine danger if he handles the conditions.

runners_data.name: Blue Faith
runners_data.comment: A Blue Point colt whose dam is a half-sister to a Group 2 winner, lending some pedigree interest on debut. The trainer has been quiet recently and the overall profile makes him difficult to fancy strongly first time out.

runners_data.name: Brondesbury
runners_data.comment: A 58,000gns Dark Angel colt who is a full brother to Green Amoro, useful at 7f, with a dam that excelled at 5f; the pedigree has appeal but this is a tough first start. The trainer is without a recent winner and he faces a demanding ask here.

races.name: Pure Panel Management Handicap (Rnd)

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Recent course winner at this trip on Good going and arrives fresh on 12 days' rest — Nigel Tinkler's 0/25 14-day record is negligible here as the yard clearly targets this spot; the lone pace-setter role is ideal tactically, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects it is placed in a lead role that is marginally outside its natural prominent bracket.
runners_data.comment: Won convincingly at Pontefract last time, pulling clear by 3¼l off a 5lb lower mark; acts well over this trip on quick ground, but now takes on a penalty with cheekpieces and the trainer’s recent record gives pause.

runners_data.name: Straight A
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's consistent five-year-old returns after 37 days and has placed four times in fifteen similar-going starts without winning; sits comfortably just off the pace and the mile on Good to Firm is squarely within its parameters, but the 0-wins from 15 similar-going runs flags a tendency to find one too good.
runners_data.comment: Shaped better than the result suggests last time, held up by a slow pace and beaten 2½l off a 1lb lower mark; effective over this trip and surface and could return to form after 37 days away, though the trainer has struggled for results recently.

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: The form string 990000 is alarming and the flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a structural liability in a race where hold-up runners need to sustain effort deep into the mile — Ben Haslam's in-form 2/14 14-day record offers some stable optimism but this horse needs to show improvement on recent running to be a factor.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in his last six starts, including after a slow beginning at Wetherby most recently; has run over this trip on a sound surface and the mark is easing, but there is plenty to prove before he can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: David O'Meara relies on Daniel Tudhope, one of the sharpest tactical riders in the north, and Al Muqdad's best recent efforts — 2nd and 3rd in its last two similar-going runs — came from the rear at seven furlongs; stepping up to a mile here could suit a horse that needs time to organise its effort.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up here last time by a nose off the same mark, showing fine form in defeat; first-time cheekpieces add interest and the trainer has a strong record at this course — the only question is whether a seven-day turnaround leaves him short.

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old has placed claims on soft and has hit the frame at this trip before, but seven of its last fifteen similar-going runs have ended in mid-division finishes; David Probert gets a good partner here if the race develops with genuine pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Placed second at Ffos Las last time, beaten half a length off a 1lb lower mark over this distance and surface; her form dipped prior to that recent effort but she returns in fair shape and has a realistic chance at best.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's four-year-old arrives on the back of a recent win and has three wins from seven similar-going starts — the best winning strike rate in this field; the apprentice rider Ethan Tindall (5) will want to use this horse's natural forward cruising speed from a handy pitch.
runners_data.comment: Won at Hamilton last time by a neck off a 3lb lower mark, digging in well to prevail; effective over today’s trip and surface, with first-time cheekpieces adding a fresh angle — though he now takes on a stiffer task off a higher mark.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and going most recently and Sam England's yard is 5/16 in the last fortnight, suggesting the stable is in a productive spell; the tongue-tie is a noted addition and Oisin Orr gets a mount that should travel naturally in the first half of the race with a genuine chance to kick clear.
runners_data.comment: Came through strongly at Redcar last time, landing a handicap by 1½l off a 6lb lower mark; effective over today’s trip on similar going, though now significantly higher in the weights — first-time tongue-tie adds interest, but a big jump forward is required.

runners_data.name: Tilani
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old has won twice consecutively and looks progressive on ratings, but its natural desire to race prominently cannot be fully satisfied here given the density of pace horses ahead of it — the redistribution to a midfield slot tempers its theoretical chance even though the underlying form is solid.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last five starts; runner-up at a longer trip last time off the same mark as today, and rated first of nine — effective from 7-10f on good ground, with the trainer’s recent form the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard has been busy (8/106 14-day) and this five-year-old has placed credentials on good ground, but its genuine hold-up tendency is further diluted by being mapped in a midfield position that suits neither its style nor the pace scenario — Jake Dickson (7) will need a genuinely strong gallop to deliver any meaningful late momentum.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Redcar most recently after some better form earlier; wears first-time cheekpieces from stall 1 and handles any ground, but stamina over this mile trip is a genuine concern given his stronger runs have come over shorter.

races.paceDynamic: Amidst The Chaos is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger to its lead, should settle into a sustainable, uncontested gallop around Doncaster's flat mile — a track that rewards horses who can dictate without burning energy in a contested early duel. Behind it, Straight A, Mwafaq, and Yafaarr are all prominent types who will compete for the positions immediately off the leader's heels, creating a naturally strung-out midfield rather than a compressed pack. The hold-up contingent of Al Muqdad, Toralou, and War Howl will be doing their racing from the rear, though War Howl's tendency to fade in the finish is a structural concern for that group. This field holds more prominent and front-running types than the map can accommodate simultaneously — Tilani and Valentine Catcher, both natural forward movers, are pushed further back than they would prefer, meaning Amidst The Chaos and the established prominent trio of Straight A, Mwafaq, and Yafaarr are most likely to actually secure those positions. A controlled, even gallop on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster strongly favours hold-up horses that can produce a sustained late run rather than a sharp turn-of-foot, but the uncontested nature of the pace means prominent racers who travel comfortably just off the lead and stay the mile genuinely are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Amidst The Chaos dictates a moderate, uncontested tempo and the prominent trio travel smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: If Amidst The Chaos dictates a moderate, uncontested tempo and the prominent trio travel smoothly throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle mile to leave prominent runners vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle mile to leave prominent runners vulnerable in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Tilani Asserts
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of prominent types causes early scrimmaging and Tilani manages to secure a better position than the map suggests.
scenarios.body: If the congestion of prominent types causes early scrimmaging and Tilani manages to secure a better position than the map suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slower than expected and Amidst The Chaos simply gallivants clear on a long rein.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slower than expected and Amidst The Chaos simply gallivants clear on a long rein.

watchPoints.text: Mwafaq and Yafaarr are both prominent types with recent wins on similar going — watch whether Ethan Tindall or Oisin Orr fires first off the turn, as the one who gets the better position entering the straight will likely have first run on the other.

Tilani's redistribution to a midfield slot is worth tracking from the gate — if Edward Greatrex pushes forward aggressively from stall draw and secures a prominent berth, its consecutive winning form makes it a live danger that the map probability undersells.

War Howl's repeated fade pattern (990000 form) suggests watching whether Andrew Mullen switches it off completely from the rear; if it is pushed too early to close, the fade could compromise finishing horses immediately behind it.
Al Muqdad was last seen just 7 days ago — watch for any signs of freshness or Tudhope deliberately hunting cover to settle the horse before delivering his challenge in the final two furlongs.

The going is reported Good to Firm for this race (despite the card header stating Good) — horses with a specific preference for cut in the ground, particularly Toralou whose best form came on Soft, may find the surface quicker than ideal.

races.name: Believe Money Group Handicap

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for George Scott who drops back to 5f on good-to-firm after a run of disappointing efforts, though his best 5f form is on good ground and Liam Wright (5) taking the ride keeps costs down; needs things to go his way from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 2l off his current mark at Brighton last time, with the trainer in good form and the weight looking manageable. Acts on any ground and goes well at 5f, but he sits towards the bottom of our figures in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old has her sole 5f win on good ground and David Nolan is an astute booking, though she is a true hold-up horse displaced into a midfield map slot because the rear is overcrowded — her chance hinges on getting a wider berth and a clean run rather than her natural position.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by a length at Thirsk last time ended a lengthy absence from the winner’s enclosure, and she comes here just 4lb higher. Consistent and effective at 5f on any ground, she rates second on our figures and remains a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old in the twilight of his career whose last recorded good-ground 5f form figures show just two placed efforts from fifteen similar-surface starts; genuinely suited to coming from behind but, shunted into midfield by the density of hold-up types, Antony Brittain's runner faces a steep task without a clean passage.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7¼l at Thirsk last time, a long way from his best, and needs to recover that form markedly to figure here. Goes well on good ground and AW at 5/6f, but he sits at the foot of our market.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby operates at a lively 7/98 over 14 days suggesting this runner arrives fit and ready; steps back to 5f from a 6f campaign and, while a natural hold-up horse forced into a midfield role by the congested rear, Duran Fentiman will be looking to switch wide and use that fresh-distance sharpness late.
runners_data.comment: Adopted a prominent position at Ripon last time and ran to his mark, beaten 4¼l; his official rating continues to ease. Effective at 5f on a sound surface and happy to front-run, but yet to score in recent starts and sits fifth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old carries a 5lb claimer (Lauren Young) and has only two placed efforts from limited good-ground starts at this distance; a genuine hold-up horse operating out of its preferred position here, and the lack of a recent win compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form at Ayr last time, though beaten 6¼l, with his official mark continuing to ease. Handles 5f on good to firm and ranks third on our figures; the trend is in his favour and he shapes as a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Paddy's Day
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and race-shaper: Nigel Tinkler's six-year-old has tumbled to OR 87 after a string of disappointing runs but the single-pace scenario here is tailor-made, and a tongue-tie is fitted; last ran just seven days ago which is a minor flag, but the absence of any pace rival is the dominant factor.
runners_data.comment: Genuine contender at 5f on this surface and the stable landed this race 12 months ago, returning here just seven days on. His effort flattened out late last time, beaten 2 lengths off this mark, but the first-time tongue-tie could prove the change he needs.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's four-year-old owns four placed efforts from five 5f runs on good ground and arrives eight days fresh — the strongest profile of any chaser in this field over this precise course-distance-going combination; Edward Greatrex gets the ride for a yard running at 3/38 over 14 days, which is a modest but not alarming strike-rate.
runners_data.comment: Effective over 5f on a sound surface and ran to form beaten 1½l off his current mark at Hamilton last time. Inclined to pull early, but that didn’t cost him and he handles the conditions; he rates the one to beat in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Paddy's Day is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise him, Alex Jary can dictate terms from the off at a tempo entirely of his choosing on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. Behind him, the field is dominated by hold-up horses — Emerald Harmony, Mondammej, Miraculous, and Oriental Prince are all natural rear-of-field types who will find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their true back-of-the-pack positions, simply because there is not enough room for all of them to settle where they want. Dyonisos and Moulin Booj also operate from off the pace, meaning the entire field outside Paddy's Day will be chasing a horse who faces zero friction in the early exchanges. This race shape strongly favours Paddy's Day and any horse with even a hint of prominent racing ability, as a single sustainable lead and a compressed chasing pack will reward those who travel closest to the action rather than those caught flat-footed at the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Paddy's Day Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Paddy's Day bowls along at a controlled, honest gallop and the hold-up pack fails to generate meaningful momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: If Paddy's Day bowls along at a controlled, honest gallop and the hold-up pack fails to generate meaningful momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Paddy's Day sets a fraction too strong for himself and ties up inside the final furlong, handing late runners a closing opportunity.
scenarios.body: If Paddy's Day sets a fraction too strong for himself and ties up inside the final furlong, handing late runners a closing opportunity.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the naturally hold-up horses — most likely Emerald Harmony or Miraculous — manages to travel wider and closer than expected, finding clear daylight.
scenarios.body: If one of the naturally hold-up horses — most likely Emerald Harmony or Miraculous — manages to travel wider and closer than expected, finding clear daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed hold-up pack fans wide, causes significant interference, and the race breaks into an unpredictable scramble with no horse travelling fluently.
scenarios.body: If the compressed hold-up pack fans wide, causes significant interference, and the race breaks into an unpredictable scramble with no horse travelling fluently.

watchPoints.text: Watch Paddy's Day in the market: if he shortens significantly at the off, his uncontested lead becomes the dominant race factor and the entire hold-up pack is immediately at a disadvantage in this 5f dash.

Monitor Emerald Harmony's drawn stall and early movement — if David Nolan pushes her forward to claim a position closer than her natural hold-up style, she becomes a live danger; if she settles in the rear as usual, her redistribution into midfield is misleading.

Dyonisos's drawn stall and early order deserve attention: with four 5f placed efforts on good ground he is the most pace-scenario-agnostic runner, capable of finishing prominently whether Paddy's Day fades or sustains the effort.

The going report confirms good-to-firm for this race despite the card listing good — that faster surface rewards a horse able to maintain a high cruising speed and slightly penalises deep hold-up tactics, reinforcing the front-runner advantage.

With five of seven runners naturally wanting to race from the rear, there is a material risk of crowding and interference in the straight; jockeys on Miraculous, Mondammej, and Oriental Prince will all be seeking the same gap at roughly the same moment.

races.name: Instarmac Group Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Military Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for David O'Meara and David Nolan, returning 22 days after a run in soft conditions where he has mixed form; his simulated-going record on good shows only two placings from eight tries and no wins, which is a genuine concern, and headgear (ht) adds a small unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held at Catterick last time, and all his better French form was on testing ground; the sound surface here is uncertain territory. Wears a first-time hood and tongue-tie; he sits at the foot of our market and has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Redbud Sixteen
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for Charlie Pike, in good heart having won twice in ten days from recent starts including a win on good ground, and Edward Greatrex's claim is useful; controls pace entirely on his own terms here, which is his biggest advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive filly who landed a handicap by 6 lengths at Newbury last time off a 6lb lower mark, asserting well clear; she comes here with a hat-trick in her sights. Effective at 1m–11f on any surface, she rates second on our figures and looks a formidable threat.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner wants to race prominently but has never won beyond 8f, stepping up to 1m2f here; Pat Dobbs rides and his best recent form has come on good ground, though the trip extension is a question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten 8l at Goodwood last time, some way short of his best, and needs to find considerably better to make an impact here. Goes on any ground and stays 12f though may be at his most effective at 8–10f; a recovery in form is required.

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for David O'Meara with a consistent record at 1m2f on good ground — ten runs at similar going, two wins, three places — but his high draw and traffic concerns from behind mean Daniel Tudhope will need a smooth passage; headgear (t) worn.|
runners_data.comment: Suited to 10–12f on a sound surface and has an easing mark, though he was well short of his best at York last time, beaten 9¼l. Wears a first-time tongue-tie; the handler has a strong record at Doncaster and a return to form makes him a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Footwork
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner has strong credentials at 1m on good ground with two wins from nine tries, and Connor Beasley settles him prominently; stepping up to 1m2f but his recent second at 9f suggests the trip should not be a barrier, and he is freshened after 34 days off.|
runners_data.comment: Posted a narrow second at his last outing 34 days ago, beaten a neck off a mark of 86, and arrives here 1lb higher. Effective at 7–9f on a sound surface and in decent shape; a midfield contender on our figures but capable of going well if reproducing that effort.

runners_data.name: Serenity Blue
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for James Horton who has shown form at 1m2f on good ground (two wins and two places from eight similar runs), though recent form figures of 09-300 are not encouraging; Jack Mitchell rides for a trainer who is 0 from 7 in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at 10–12f on a sound surface, but he has cut a poor figure in recent outings and a marked upturn is needed. Wears first-time cheekpieces and sits third on our figures; the new gear is the reason to give him another look.

runners_data.name: Be Patient
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's lightly-raced three-year-old has run only twice, winning on debut at 8f on standard and placing next time; 239 days off and stepping up significantly in trip to 1m2f on faster ground than seen before makes this a major unknown, but Oisin Orr's booking signals stable confidence.|
runners_data.comment: On the back of a narrow novice success at Newcastle, he returns after a 239-day break and steps up in trip to 10f for the first time. All his form is on AW; the handicap debut holds some appeal, but significant fitness questions need answering.

runners_data.name: Bintknight
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's three-year-old has won once at 1m on good ground and is a true hold-up type by style — displaced to midfield on the map solely because the field is congested with hold-up horses; Lewis Edmunds claims, and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 means its chance is tempered if it cannot access its natural position at the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Showed clear progression from debut when landing her maiden at Lingfield last time by a neck despite a slow beginning. Effective at 10f on good ground and now taking her chance on a handicap debut off a mark that looks fair; our figures make her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — confirm at declaration; Simon & Ed Crisford's runner had placed form at 1m on good ground and was stepping up in trip, but this entry must be treated as void until scratching is officially confirmed.|

races.paceDynamic: Redbud Sixteen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him, is likely to dictate at a sustainable gallop from the outset, controlling tempo through the first half of this 1m2f trip on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. Footwork and Eupator will press forward prominently behind him, and with Be Patient also wanting an early position, there is meaningful congestion two to three furlongs out as the field enters the straight — creating a wall of horses that could compromise straightforward passage for those tracking them. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly; Bintknight is a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping, and while Prince Of The Seas and Military Air are true closers, the congestion in the straight makes clean runs uncertain for all of them. A measured, uncontested pace set by Redbud Sixteen favours prominent racers who can travel economically just behind him and pounce early in the straight before the wider field has organised — the prominent profile is best placed here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Redbud Sixteen Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Redbud Sixteen is allowed to set an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent trio cannot sustain their challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Redbud Sixteen is allowed to set an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent trio cannot sustain their challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Gaggle Quickens Past Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Footwork, Eupator, or Be Patient push up aggressively from the early stages and force a stronger gallop that overruns Redbud Sixteen.
scenarios.body: If Footwork, Eupator, or Be Patient push up aggressively from the early stages and force a stronger gallop that overruns Redbud Sixteen.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners tie each other up and slow patches in the straight create gaps for hold-up horses to exploit.
scenarios.body: If the prominent runners tie each other up and slow patches in the straight create gaps for hold-up horses to exploit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Creates Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses dispute the lead from the start, scrambling the tempo and producing a chaotic finish with no horse dominant.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent horses dispute the lead from the start, scrambling the tempo and producing a chaotic finish with no horse dominant.

watchPoints.text: Redbud Sixteen: if he escapes unpressured through the first three furlongs, the pace could be too slow to inconvenience him and he may simply coast home — monitor whether Footwork or Eupator attempts to challenge early.|

Traffic danger 2-3 furlongs out: with four horses competing for prominent positions behind the leader, there is a high probability of a bunched straight and horses checking or switching — Prince Of The Seas and Military Air are most vulnerable to a blocked run.|

Be Patient: 239 days off, a significant trip extension, and unproven on faster ground — if the pace quickens materially, this three-year-old may lack the fitness to sustain its effort; watch the market for clues about stable confidence.|
Colourband is listed as a non-runner — verify officially before the off, as a confirmed scratch reduces the field to 8 and slightly eases the congestion behind the leader.|

Bintknight's redistribution means its true hold-up role may be compromised if there is no clear rail or gap to aim for in the straight — Lewis Edmunds' inexperience at this level is an additional watch point if racing out of its preferred position.|

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap

runners_data.name: Ishe Worth Agamble
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old shows a consistent recent form of placing at this exact trip on Good ground, but its natural hold-up style means in this low-pace race it will be ridden further forward than ideal, blunting its finishing kick; headgear (tp) suggests it needs to be switched on, and at 12 days since last run it is fresh.
runners_data.comment: Slow to break at Pontefract last time and well beaten; wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time today, with his mark continuing to slide — the earlier form showed more promise, but significant improvement is needed here.

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's four-year-old returns after 35 days off and has placed at this course and distance before, but is a genuine sit-and-wait type who will be pushed into a position mid-race that doesn't suit its strengths — the absence of a searching gallop makes a big run unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Hampered by having to go wide from a difficult position at Carlisle last time and beaten 5l; showed decent form prior to that, acts over today’s 6f trip on good ground — a cleaner passage could see him perform better.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Clarets
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride on Fahey's three-year-old who has placed in back-to-back 6f handicaps on Good and Standard, visored and in form — a true hold-up horse but one with the class to sit close enough off this pace that the position compromise is manageable; best chance of the deeper-drawn horses.
runners_data.comment: Below par here last time, beaten 6½l, but his April form suggests he remains on a fair mark; wears a visor for the first time today over 6f on sound ground — if the new headgear sparks a response, he has a genuine case.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope's booking is significant for O'Meara's three-year-old, who ran second over this exact trip on Good ground last time and handles the conditions well; visor applied and racing off just 7 days, it is a natural hold-up runner but Tudhope will be alive to the need to sit closer than usual off a single front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Narrowly denied at this course last week, going down by a neck off a 1lb higher mark than today’s; wears a first-time visor with a trainer who has an excellent course record — needs to build on that effort, but a win looks overdue.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's three-year-old has an unknown style rating and has been off 60 days, with a last-time-out run of ninth over 6f on Good — limited similar-going form (1 run, no wins or places) makes this a significant unknown quantity and the trainer's 14-day record of 1/6 offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Ninth at Windsor last time and beaten 4½l, before a 60-day absence; drops in trip today and needs to settle better, acts at 7f and mainly on artificial surfaces — these conditions represent something of an unknown, and a fluent run is the key.

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Tony Culhane & Stella Barclay's three-year-old has best form at 7f and its two placed efforts came at that trip — dropping to 6f, this natural closer is already stretching its comfort zone, and the redistribution to midfield in this scenario means it is racing both out of trip and out of natural position simultaneously.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in his last three outings after a promising placed effort; sound ground here suits him as his form has only materialised on those surfaces, but a long run without threatening the principals makes him difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Maxi Boy
runners_data.note: Fionn McSharry's nine-year-old carries top weight of 142lbs and is a genuine hold-up type whose recent form over 6f on Similar-going tracks shows just one place from five — the weight burden and a career high-class field at this age make it a tough ask, even if the pace were to suit.
runners_data.comment: Disappointed at Chester last time but effective over today’s trip and surface; his speed figures are solid and he has shown better form earlier in the season — a return to form would put him among the threats here.

runners_data.name: Carlton And Co
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in the race, Michael & David Easterby's seven-year-old has won over this exact trip on Standard ground recently and has strong course and distance form; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects it is being mapped as prominent rather than truly leading, but it is the race-controlling force here and Joanna Mason's front-running tactics are well-established.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Hamilton last time on a trip that went well beyond her comfort zone; first-time visor and a return to 6f are both potential pluses for a mare with ability over shorter, and she is worth considering.

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old wears a hood (p) and has the most consistent recent form in the field at 6-7f on Good ground, logging five consecutive placed or near-placed efforts — naturally a sit-and-wait type, but the headgear and Dale Swift's positional awareness make it the redistributed horse most likely to push forward and complicate the lead picture.
runners_data.comment: Out of form in his last six starts but has been dropping to what may be an appealing mark; wears cheekpieces over a trip that suits him on fitting ground — a return to form could make him competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Carlton And Co is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Joanna Mason's seven-year-old should secure a uncontested rail berth and set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over this straight Doncaster six furlongs. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the race will be run at a measured tempo in the early stages before the sprint kicks in from the two-furlong pole — a shape that heavily favours runners who can travel handy and quicken, rather than deep closers needing a strong pace to reel in the leader. Kings Merchant, Ishe Worth Agamble, Get Up Everybody and Go Victor are all genuine hold-up horses in nature, but with the midfield and rear so congested the map cannot accommodate them all — Kings Merchant, given his prominent headgear (p) and trainer's handling, is the most likely to push into a forward position, while the others are unlikely to reach their natural station. This race shape — a lone, unhurried pace-setter on fast ground with a field stuffed with closers who will struggle to find clear air — firmly favours horses racing prominently or capable of a prominent pitch, able to stalk the front-runner and deliver their effort without needing a deep gallop to produce them.

watchPoints.text: Carlton And Co's ability to get away cleanly from the stalls is critical — if Joanna Mason gets an uncontested lead, the race shape locks in immediately; watch the first furlong to see whether any other runner challenges for the front.

Kings Merchant's early positioning will be decisive — if Dale Swift elects to press forward aggressively rather than drop in, the controlled pace scenario fractures and several other runners' tactics become redundant.

The congested midfield of redistributed hold-up horses (Ishe Worth Agamble, Get Up Everybody, Go Victor, Kings Merchant) creates a real risk of interference in the straight at Doncaster — watch for traffic issues inside the final two furlongs.

Good to Firm ground confirmed for this race suits front-runners and prominent racers at Doncaster's straight six — horses with proven form on Fast-side going (Carlton And Co, Cosmic Clarets, Come On Over) have a meaningful surface edge over those whose best runs came on Soft or Standard.

Maxi Boy's 142lbs top weight is the highest in the field by a significant margin — monitor whether Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) can offset any weight disadvantage, as the claimer booking may be a deliberate tactical move by connections to manage the burden.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Chicory
runners_data.note: Returned to winning ways over 6f on good recently (form 170-72 reversed to include that win), but steps back to 5f here — Ed Walker's hold-up filly will need the pace to stretch in order to deploy her finish, and the lone front-runner scenario makes that uncertain; Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking.
runners_data.comment: Finished second at Nottingham last time, beaten 2½l off a 1lb higher mark when tried over 5f; back at that same trip here and the conditions look ideal. Effective at 5/6f on good ground and our top-rated runner, she has every reason to go well here.

runners_data.name: Saffron Dandy
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon three-year-old whose recent form on good-to-firm at 6f (sim-going 0W0P in 10 runs) raises legitimate doubts about her ability to translate form to these conditions; drops to 5f for the first time in winning form, and her hold-up style leaves her relying on a pace that may simply not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by a neck at Goodwood last time off a 1lb lower mark, she comes here just 1lb higher after a 21-day break. Effective at 5/6f on a sound surface and the form suggests she can go in again after a small penalty.

runners_data.name: Cressida Wildes
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's visor-wearing four-year-old won over this C&D on soft, but her true racing style is closer to hold-up than the midfield slot the map allocates her; the switch to good-to-firm and the absence of genuine pace may leave her with too much to do from her actual finishing position, though 1W3P in 15 sim-going starts shows she fires on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Well below her best at Yarmouth last time and has managed to pass only one rival across her four most recent outings; a first-time visor is the obvious change. Suited to 5f on a sound surface but sits at the foot of our figures and needs a significant turnaround.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's four-year-old arrives on a seven-day turnaround having finished a respectable fourth last time, and her form string of 3-3-3 placements speaks to a consistent but hard-to-win profile; her natural instinct is to come from off the pace, which the race shape actively penalises here, and the three-pound claim for Christian Howarth is the one mitigating factor.
runners_data.comment: Despite an awkward break from the stalls last time, she ran to her mark and finished just 1¼l adrift here at Doncaster. Effective at 5/6f on a sound surface and running off a competitive official mark; she holds a reasonable each-way chance if repeating that effort.

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old is the pivotal tactical piece — a genuine prominent racer who won over 6f on good and has the gate speed to track Eternal Sunshine throughout; Harry Davies has ridden this filly before and will know to position her early, making her the most naturally suited runner to the race shape if the leader stops.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just a nose last time off a mark of 75, edged out late having gone freely early; she comes here 1lb higher. Suited by 6f on a sound surface and admirably consistent; she ranks third on our figures and remains a clear danger to the selection.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Won twice over course-and-distance on good ground and arrives here as the most proven 5f performer in the field on similar going (2W4P in 10 runs); a true hold-up runner placed in midfield by redistribution, but her recent winning habits and low weight of 124lbs are genuine assets if she can find clear running — Dougie Costello's experience in tight finishes is relevant.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by a neck at Thirsk last time showed the right attitude and she arrives in fine form, now 4lb higher. At her best over 5f on a sound surface; she is fifth on our figures but a solid each-way prospect if the rise proves manageable.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner and faces a career-high weight of 142lbs, which is a genuine stamina concern over 5f on fast ground; her recent form shows she has been running into midfield positions (9th, 10th, 13th) and the STYLE_FIT flag is warranted — her ability to sustain the lead is the pivotal question, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight burden.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with renewed purpose at Ayr last time, beaten 2l off this mark, suggesting she is approaching her best again. Handles 5/6f on any going and rates second on our figures; her record on good ground is particularly strong and she is the principal danger here.

runners_data.name: Alpine Girl
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's six-year-old has a remarkable C&D record (5W in good-ground 5f form) and is the most course-proven runner in the field, but a 47-day absence and a trainer who has gone 0/17 in the last fortnight are significant context flags; wearing hood, she is a natural hold-up filly racing in a shape that does not reward her style, though raw ability means she cannot be ignored if the race falls apart in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Successful in this race 12 months ago but below her best last time, beaten 8l off a 2lb higher mark; she drops 2lb here and a first-time hood is the obvious change. Effective at 5/6f on a sound surface but ranks low on our figures and needs to lift her game.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Sunshine is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f handicap and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she should bowl along unchallenged from the gates on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. The pace she sets is therefore likely to be honest but controlled — a lone leader dictating her own rhythm without the energy cost of a duel, which is the most favourable scenario for a front-runner on a flat, sharp track. Space Bear is the only other runner with a genuinely prominent profile and will likely slot in just off the leader's flank, adding a second marker but not enough to turn this into a true scorcher. This shape — a single uncontested pace-setter on quick ground over a minimum trip — strongly favours horses who race on or close to the pace, as the early fractions will not be severe enough to cause the leader to tie up and there will be limited time for hold-up horses to close. This field contains more hold-up types than the track can accommodate naturally: Cressida Wildes, Alondra, Alpine Girl, and Dragon Spin are all true hold-up runners; with the pace insufficient to string the field out, those four will be compressed in a midfield group and only the sharpest of finishers among them will reach the winner's enclosure.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Sunshine's weight of 142lbs is the most pressing concern in the race — if she tires inside the final furlong after setting her own pace, Space Bear is perfectly placed to inherit and the entire race shape pivots on that single moment.

Dragon Spin is 124lbs and arrives with two wins over course-and-distance on good ground; at the widest draw, Dougie Costello will need to find a clean passage early, and any interference from the compressed hold-up group could cost her the race in the short sprint.

Alpine Girl's 47-day absence for a trainer on 0/17 in recent form is a tangible risk flag — she has the class to win but freshness over 5f on fast ground requires an immediate peak, and the hood may or may not sharpen her enough.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race despite the official card showing Good — a meaningful difference that favours horses who have proven form on quick ground; Cressida Wildes and Chicory both show sim-going positives on fast surfaces, while Saffron Dandy's 0W0P on comparable going is a material concern.

With four of the eight runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types forced into midfield, traffic at the two-furlong marker is a near certainty — any horse drawn wide or slow away risks being completely shut out of the finish, making early position more valuable than usual in this compressed field.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Bami
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner; recent win at this trip on Good ground fits perfectly and Tom Dascombe's yard is 1 from 12 in the 14-day window — she should dictate terms but her [STYLE_FIT] tag signals she is racing outside her most comfortable role and any pressure applied early could undermine her.
runners_data.comment: Won at Newbury last time with real determination, landing a handicap by ¾l off a 6lb lower mark; effective over today’s trip and surface and rates well enough to hold her own under the penalty — the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Why Because
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley hold-up filly who drops back to 7f from a run of 8f outings, 43 days off and no wins on similar going in six attempts — David Nolan takes the ride but the form profile offers little encouragement for a win here.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Catterick last time on her return to form, beaten 5½l in a maiden; the step up to 7f could play to her strengths and she dons a first-time hood, but she is yet to score in recent starts and the trainer’s form is modest.

runners_data.name: Borjina
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old ran a storming 1st on good ground over 7f and sits in a prominent position she can naturally fill; Oisin Orr is a smart judge of pace and 29 days between runs is a normal freshener — she looks exactly the type this race shape favours.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Wetherby last time, unable to get into contention from off the pace; has won over 7f on good ground and showed ability in the run before that setback — a recovery would make her a factor.

runners_data.name: Seeing Stars
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with four placed efforts over 7f and a win at this trip on Soft — her record on this particular going band is thin (1 from 6) but Harry Davies rides confidently and her relentless consistency from a forward berth makes her hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and beaten just 2l at Wetherby last time, facing 1lb more than today’s mark; effective over 7f on fast ground and AW, with a win in her recent starts — a genuine threat with solid each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partner has been running over shorter of late and the step up from sprint trips is unproven; hold-up style is genuine but her recent form figures of 7-9446 suggest she is struggling to find her level.
runners_data.comment: Ex-French and showing some ability for her new yard, but beaten 5¼l last time and rated lowest of the field by our measure; the trainer has a strong record at this track, though it would take a marked improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K R Burke hold-up filly returning after 68 days off — her placed efforts over 7f on Soft and Stan are encouraging and she has the best going record of the hold-up brigade, but a two-month absence on this quick surface needs accounting for.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Nottingham last time, beaten 3l off a 1lb higher mark; returns after 68 days away and is effective over this distance on good ground — some freshness from the break may help, but she has yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Accademia
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has a legitimate hold-up style that places her deeper than her map position suggests, and her form of 744-5 at 7f on comparable going shows she has yet to convert; Kieran Shoemark's booking is a plus but the redistribution leaves her racing in a less comfortable spot than she would choose.
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Lingfield last time and beaten 6l there; consistently placed in recent starts but yet to score, and she may have more to offer over today’s trip — place claims are realistic if she takes a step forward.

runners_data.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners_data.note: Arrives in red-hot form with back-to-back wins on good ground, including this trip, and is the hold-up horse with the most compelling recent credentials; Joanna Mason rides and her course-form record of 2W3P in 12 similar-going runs makes her the standout deeper threat.
runners_data.comment: Won here last time by a head off a 4lb lower mark, sealing back-to-back wins with a resolute effort; effective over today’s trip and surface, she bids for a hat-trick off a raised mark — the key question is whether she can repeat from a wide draw.

runners_data.name: South Coast Star
runners_data.note: David Probert partner showed improvement winning over this exact course and distance on Tapeta last time — the prominent style suits the race shape and Hugo Palmer's yard is in decent form, though the jump from Tapeta to Good to Firm turf is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Won at Wolverhampton last time by 6l off a 9lb lower mark with plenty in hand; trainer in form and she is effective over today’s trip, but a significant rise in the weights and the switch to turf are the questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up filly whose true position is further back than the map places her; Conrad Allen has had zero winners from four runners in the 14-day window and form of 74-364 gives limited confidence, though the trip is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Lingfield last time over a mile, staying on but inclined to pull; a drop in trip today may be a plus and she handles sound surfaces, but she is yet to score in recent starts and needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner who has headgear noted, six runs on similar going (1 win, 2 placed) and creditable recent form — her natural closing style finds her mapped forward of where she would settle, and that positional compromise could blunt her finishing effort in a race not run strongly enough.
runners_data.comment: Third last time, beaten 7l off the same mark she meets here, finding little when pressure was applied; wears first-time cheekpieces and handles the trip and going, but needs more pace to trouble the leaders.

runners_data.name: Uncertainty
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's three-year-old has struggled for consistency with figures of 4-8797, and six appearances on good ground have yielded zero wins — her deep hold-up style is real but the lack of acceleration in her recent form makes her an unlikely beneficiary even if the pace is genuine.

races.paceDynamic: Bami is the confirmed front runner here and, with only South Coast Star, Borjina, and Seeing Stars likely to push forward alongside her, this shapes as a sustainably-paced gallop rather than a scorching test — Good to Firm ground at Doncaster's straight seven furlongs will reward those who travel smoothly and kick late off a genuine but measured pace. Bami has the beating of her nearest rivals for early position and should control tempo from the front, meaning the race will not fall apart early and the field will compress into the straight before the decisive moves come. That controlled pace over 7f on quick ground suits prominent racers who can sit just behind the leader and pounce, rather than true closers who need a lung-busting gallop to peg back the front rank. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the map accommodates — Accademia, Uncertainty, Angel Summer, and Vega's Virtue are genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their natural rear position, with Borjina, Seeing Stars, and South Coast Star the prominent racers most likely to occupy the chasing positions directly behind Bami.

watchPoints.text: Bami's lead could be challenged earlier than expected by Borjina and Seeing Stars — if those two press her hard from the off, the pace could accelerate beyond what Bami's natural rhythm can sustain, fundamentally altering the race shape.

Gunalt Wavelength arrives with back-to-back wins on good ground at 7f and Joanna Mason will be aiming to produce her late — any horse drawn wider than ideal could see her arrive with a flourish if the prominent runners have briefly gone too hard.

South Coast Star's form was achieved on Tapeta at the same course — punters and traders should watch whether the step onto Good to Firm turf surfaces any ground concern in her early movement, as this is the biggest unknown about her participation.

Several redistributed hold-up horses (Accademia, Angel Summer, Uncertainty, Vega's Virtue) will be competing for positions they do not naturally seek — watch the early stalls to see which, if any, pop out quickly and accidentally force their way into a forward spot, which would further congest the prominent group.
